newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-JURY RULES IN FAVOR OF FORMER TYSON TRAINER.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-JURY RULES IN FAVOR OF FORMER TYSON TRAINER.

text.p: A jury awarded $4.1 million Monday to Kevin Rooney, former trainer of heavyweight bxing champion Mike Tyson, in a contract dispute with the fighter.
The federal court jury in Albany, which deliberated for more than nine hours over two days before reaching the verdict, also decided that Tyson did not prove just cause to fire Rooney in 1988.
Tyson, who was sued for $49 million by Rooney, described the verdict as "ridiculous" and said, "if Kevin would have asked me for four million dollars I would have given it to him".

Rooney had accused the boxer in the lawsuit of failing to honour a verbal contract made to him by Tyson's late mentor, Cus D'Amato, promising him a lifetime job with a guaranteed 10 percent cut of the boxer's winnings. Tyson's attorney had countered that the boxer knew nothing about such a contract.

"I'm satisfied," Rooney told reporters at the courthouse. "I never expected 49 million but you can't take blood from a stone. They came in with what they feel is a just verdict and I'm not going to argue with it."
